authoredSolutions.82: The four distinct digits include \(7\) as the largest, the other three coming from \(\{0,1,\dots,6\}\). Since the first two digits and the last two have equal sum, the four digits split into two pairs of equal sum, one pair containing \(7\). Pairing \(7\) with \(x\) forces the remaining two digits to sum to \(7+x\); the number of valid pairs is \(3,2,2,1,1\) for \(x=0,1,2,3,4\), i.e. \(9\) digit-configurations. Each configuration gives \(2\times2\times2=8\) codes (which pair occupies the first two places, and the order within each pair), so the number of possible codes is \(9\times8=72\).
